Summary: A 65-year-old male with a history of sarcoidosis and diabetes mellitus presents with chronic anicteric cholestasis and Budd-Chiari syndrome complicating sarcoidosis. Key findings include chronic anicteric cholestasis, jaundice, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, and elevated γ-glutamyl transferase, ALP, and inflammatory anemia. Procedures performed include abdominal ultrasound and CT, and medications discharged are oral prednisolone and warfarin. Follow-up instructions include regular primary care physician and specialist appointments, monitoring symptoms, adherence to medications, and lifestyle modifications.

Initial Clinical Summary:

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a primary diagnosis of Left cerebellopontine angle (CPA) lipoma, a secondary diagnosis of 37-dB hearing loss in the left ear with 70% speech discrimination, and a critical lab abnormality of 37-dB hearing loss. He has undergone radiological examinations and is prescribed further testing (CT/MRI) by an otolaryngologist. Follow-up instructions include visiting an otolaryngologist for further evaluation and testing.

Summary:

The patient is experiencing cardiac failure and nonischemic cardiomyopathy. They are also in ECOG performance status 3 with mediastinal widening, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, cellulitis, neutropenic fevers, and pseudomonas aeruginosa infection. Additionally, they have protracted nausea and vomiting.

Procedures performed include mechanical cardiac support with an LVAD, mediastinoscopy. Medications discharged include carboplatin, IV etoposide, and chemotherapy.

Follow-up instructions include hospice care and discharge home.

Summary:

The patient is diagnosed with Postradiogenic circumscribed scleroderma (morphea) and carcinoma of the right breast. Additionally, she has axillary lymph nodes involvement and radiodermatitis with moist epitheliolysis, circumscribed cutis edema, and RTX. She is undergoing adjuvant RTX and needs to follow up with her doctors for scheduled checkups, monitor her affected areas, and avoid sun exposure and use sunscreen.

Summary: A 65-year-old female patient is admitted with IgA nephropathy, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and end-stage renal disease. She also has sensorineural hearing loss, proteinuria, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets, and microalbuminuria. The patient underwent a kidney biopsy and peritoneal dialysis. She is currently on prednisone, tacrolimus, and is scheduled for follow-up with a nephrologist.

Summary:

A 52-year-old male patient presenting with suspected vascular injury in the neck zone II due to multiple cervicofacial lacerations. The patient's blood pressure is critically low (70/40 mmHg) and pulse is elevated (110 beats/minute), indicating shock. Hemoglobin level is low (4.7 mg/dl), suggesting severe anemia.

Procedures: CT angiography, angiography via the right femoral artery, stent insertion, and surgery to remove the hematoma.

Medications: Antiplatelet medication.

Follow-up instructions: Continue antiplatelet medication and attend follow-up appointments at our outpatient clinic.

Summary: The patient is diagnosed with CML in chronic phase, pancytopenia, leishmaniasis, and acute cardiac toxicity. They have splenomegaly, high leukocyte count, low hemoglobin level, and high platelet count. Hydroxyurea, imatinib, pentavalent antimonials, and TKI therapy are prescribed for treatment. Follow up as needed after discharge.

Summary:

A 45-year-old male patient with recurrent pneumonia, lymphadenopathy, and enlarged liver and spleen, has been diagnosed with CD hyaline vascular type. He is currently undergoing treatment with prednisone, azathioprine, colchicine, and rivaroxaban. Follow-up is scheduled with the rheumatology outpatient department.

Summary: A 35-year-old female patient with central keratitis and corneal scraping diagnosed with Acanthamoeba sp. cysts. She is on alternating topical fortified vancomycin, ceftazidime, propamidine isothionate 0.1%, and chlorhexidine. Follow-up instructions include no growth identified after inoculation of corneal scraping specimen onto E. coli plated NNA agar.

Summary:

A 32-year-old female patient presented with pituitary germinoma, central diabetes insipidus, hypopituitarism, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, polyuria, and hypertonic hypernatremia. She underwent MRI scan, hydrocortisone and levothyroxine replacement therapy, tissue biopsy, water deprivation test, and whole ventricle brain radiation. The patient is currently receiving medications for hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and hypertonic hypernatremia and is scheduled for follow-up visits with the endocrinology clinic to monitor treatment and evaluate persistent symptoms.

Initial Clinical Summary:

The patient is experiencing cognitive impairment and AD-like hypometabolic pattern, with the primary diagnoses of Alzheimer's disease. Secondary conditions are absent. Key abnormal lab findings include tau, ptau, and Aβ1-42 levels. Procedures performed include MMSE, MoCA-B, CDR, global deterioration scale, cerebrospinal fluid tau, ptau, Aβ1-42 level testing, Pittsburg compound B positron emission tomography (PET) scan, and F-18 fluorodeoxyglucose PET scan. Follow-up instructions include a primary care provider for continued management of cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.

Summary:

A 45-year-old female patient with a history of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma was admitted to the hospital for evaluation and management of her symptoms. She presented with fever, headache, and high blood pressure. Multiple tumor occupations were found in the left adrenal and paraganglion region zones, and appropriate medications were administered for symptom management. Follow-up instructions include continued follow-up and monitoring of the lesions for potential further treatment.

Summary: A 14-year-old female presents with a history of bone loss and apex constrained maxillary right canine, requiring orthodontic treatment. Following surgical removal of the maxillary right canine and partial maxillary osteotomy, elastic traction is administered for 21 days. Intermaxillary immobilization is prescribed for 21 days, followed by weekly postoperatory controls with orthodontic arch-wire substitution for 10 years and 10 months.

Summary: The patient presents with chest pain and lightheadedness. Further evaluation revealed pleuritic chest pain, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and no critical lab abnormalities. No procedures were performed, and no medications were discharged. The patient is advised to follow up with a cardiologist and a primary care physician for further management and to resume regular medication regimen.

Summary:
A 25-year-old female patient with a history of sodium hydroxide splash injury of left eye and symblepharon with superficial and deep corneal neovascularization is admitted for treatment. She also has a corneal epithelial defect, stromal edema, and descemet’s folds. Treatment involves subconjunctival bevacizumab injection, subconjunctival bevacizumab injection, dexamethasone sodium phosphate drops, atropine drops, tobramycin, and prednisone 50mg for ten days. Follow-up is scheduled for 24 months later.

Summary: The patient is diagnosed with Stage IV pulmonary adenocarcinoma, with accompanying lymphadenopathy in the left neck, mediastinum, and a tubercle in the right lung. Treatment involves transbronchial needle aspiration biopsy, endobronchial ultrasonography, mediastinal lymphadenectomy, wedge resection of the lower lobe of the right lung, and follow-up MRI. The patient continues on treatment and remains asymptomatic, 31 months after initiation of pembrolizumab.

Summary:

The patient is experiencing heart failure due to a combination of a renal artery aneurysm and an arteriovenous fistula. Elevated B-type Natriuretic Peptide (BNP) levels indicate cardiac dysfunction. Key findings include renal artery aneurysm, arteriovenous fistula, and heart failure. Procedures performed include endovascular occlusion. Medications are being continued, and the patient is instructed to follow up with the primary care physician for further evaluation and management of heart failure and renal artery aneurysm.

The patient has been diagnosed with HBV cirrhosis without HDV coinfection, oesophageal varices, and elevated ALT values, ALT at 3.1 ULN, HBV-DNA levels at 5.75 log10, 9.2 log10, 8.3 log10, and prothrombin time at 47%. Liver biopsy has been performed. The patient is currently listed for liver transplantation as the treatment of HBV cirrhosis.

Summary:

Patient presented with multiple congenital anomalies including abnormal genitalia, impotence, and gastrointestinal complications. Key findings include double penis and hypospadias, imperforate anus, duplicated bowel loops, and duplicated recto-sigmoid colon.

Procedures performed: laparotomy, colostomy, cystoplasty, and surgical exploration.

Medications discharged: none.

Follow-up instructions: Parents should schedule regular follow-up appointments with the primary care physician for monitoring and management of the condition. They should also discuss any further diagnostic or treatment options with the healthcare provider if necessary. It is essential to follow a healthy diet and hygiene practices to prevent complications and discomfort.

Summary: The patient is undergoing infertility treatment due to polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). She has been diagnosed with high anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) levels, which are critical lab abnormalities. A laparoscopic-assisted myomectomy has been performed for her condition. Medications will be discontinued and she will be advised to follow-up during her next routine visit.

Summary: A 35-year-old male patient with a history of tuberculosis (TB) presented with a paradoxical reaction to the prescribed antituberculosis medication regimen. The patient's primary diagnosis is paradoxical reaction, which is a rare adverse reaction to certain medications. The patient's secondary conditions are not specified. The patient's critical lab abnormalities are not mentioned. The patient's procedures performed were a CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy. The medications discharged include isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, and levofloxacin. Follow-up instructions are to continue on the prescribed antituberculosis therapy and to follow up with the healthcare provider as needed.

Initial Clinical Summary:

A 55-year-old male presented with a 6-month history of a rapidly growing, painless nodule on the right upper extremity. The patient is a former smoker with a history of tobacco use. A 2-cm excisional biopsy was performed, and the diagnosis of primary cutaneous ALCL was established. The patient is scheduled for follow-up with the oncology team as directed.

The patient has RVOT-VT with chest pain and palpitations, which is associated with obstructive coronary artery disease. The patient has undergone external cardioversion, intravenous amiodarone, coronary artery bypass grafting, and subcutaneous ICD placement. The patient is currently on medications such as aspirin, atorvastatin, digoxin, lisinopril, and spironolactone-hydrochlorothiazide. Follow-up instructions include returning to primary care physician and specialists as needed.

Summary:

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted with oral Crohn's disease without intestinal manifestations. The primary diagnosis is oral Crohn's disease. Secondary conditions are low serum iron and folate levels, and raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Critical lab abnormalities are low serum iron and folate levels, raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate. The patient underwent external gingivectomy, which resulted in oral ulcerations and lip swelling responding to treatment. Follow-up instructions are to follow up for 15 months and repeat hematological tests to monitor for any changes in the initial findings.

Summary: Patient is experiencing difficulty flushing the PEG tube, localized PEG-tube site pain, and an external bulge at the gastrostomy site. The PEG tube is also prone to external migration. No further hospital follow-up is required.

Summary: The patient is diagnosed with CMT and has a right-sided chest wall mass. The tumor was excised during a right posterolateral thoracotomy, and the patient's SCM tendon was released. Follow-up instructions are provided by oncology.

Summary: Patient is undergoing treatment for Chronic pain syndrome with failed back surgery syndrome (FBSS). The patient has a mixed pain syndrome with neuropathic radicular and nociceptive components in the lower back. They are undergoing spinal cord stimulation (SCS) for pain management. Follow-up instructions include regular reprogramming visits and maintenance of neuromodulation systems.

Summary:

This patient presents with a complex medical history consisting of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), Diabetes Mellitus type 2, and High cholesterol. Additionally, they have several secondary conditions including Exertional dyspnea, Visual disturbances, Night sweats, and Progressive fatigue. Key findings include elevated White blood cell count, low Hemoglobin, and dangerously low Platelets. 

Procedures performed include Leukapheresis and Chemotherapy and ATRA. The patient is currently taking medications for their conditions. 

Follow-up instructions include adhering to regular follow-up care as prescribed by the healthcare provider.

The patient has poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with squamous features suggestive of pancreaticobiliary primary. Secondary conditions include generalized body weakness, difficulty sleeping, abdominal pain, increased thirst with urinary frequency, constipation, elevated leukocytosis, elevated corrected calcium levels, elevated alkaline phosphatase levels, normal phosphorus levels, low vitamin D levels, high PTHrP levels, normal kidney function, and percutaneous transhepatic cholecystostomy (PTC) performed.

Summary: Patient diagnosed with MD gene panel, secondary condition of palpitation, elevated CK levels, and ongoing systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Follow up instructions include continuing SLE medications, scheduling appointment with cardiology for palpitation monitoring, and genetic counseling for the VUS variant.

Summary: A 30-year-old female presented with a suspected ZIKV infection and contact lens intolerance. Urine and blood samples were collected for diagnosis. Her condition is under active surveillance, and she is advised to seek medical attention if any future concerns related to her condition arise. Further management was deferred.

Summary:

A 55-year-old male patient presented with small-cell lung cancer and acute idiopathic pericarditis. His follow-up plan includes urgent transthoracic echocardiography, emergency pericardiocentesis, and resuming chemo-radiation therapy 2 months after discharge. The patient is also advised to discontinue tobacco abuse.

Summary: A 14-year-old female with a primary diagnosis of PTSD and a secondary diagnosis of suicidal ideation was discharged home following individual and family therapy sessions. The patient was also scheduled to attend a youth Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) the following week to receive ongoing therapy and support in managing her PTSD.

Summary: A 45-year-old female presented with invasive low-grade carcinoma of the appendix colonizing appendicial endometriosis. She underwent right hemicolectomy, resection of two segments of small intestine, omentectomy, bilateral ovariectomy, and peritoneal resections with HIPEC administration. Close outpatient follow-up is recommended.

Summary: A 35-year-old female patient is admitted with incomplete duplication of the right side, characterized by left hydronephrosis and hydroureter. She has undergone Cohen's ureteroneocystostomy and is advised to follow up with the physician for regular check-ups. No further treatment is required at this time.

Summary: A 17-year-old male patient diagnosed with B-cell ALL is being treated for a CNS relapse and second relapse. He is undergoing induction chemotherapy, double-delayed intensification, maintenance therapy, whole brain irradiation, whole spine irradiation, and aggressive reinduction chemotherapy. Follow up instructions include regular monitoring of leukemia progression and adherence to medication regimen.

Summary: A 45-year-old male patient is diagnosed with chronic bronchitis, bronchial anthracofibrosis, and tuberculous pleuritis. Chest pain and shortness of breath are the primary reasons for the encounter. The patient is also experiencing a pleural effusion and granulomatous inflammation of the right parietal pleura. Treatment involves anti-tuberculosis therapy and regular follow-up with the primary care physician.

Summary:

The patient presents with multifocal pneumonia, which is characterized by the presence of multiple lung abscesses. The patient's vital signs indicate persistent fevers, which are indicative of an ongoing infection. Additional pathogens identified in the patient's blood culture include Pneumocystis jiroveci, Cytomegalovirus, Herpes simplex virus, E. faecalis, K. pneumoniae, and P. wickerhamii.

Key findings include the presence of multiple abscesses in the lungs and elevated temperatures, indicating an ongoing infectious process. The patient has been prescribed IV antibiotics, including clindamycin, gancyclovir, linezolid, ceftaroline, ampicillin, valacyclovir, and amphotericin B.

The patient is instructed to continue regular medical treatment and medication regimen, and to discuss any concerns or changes in symptoms with their healthcare provider. Follow-up care is scheduled with the primary care provider to ensure the patient remains stable and to adjust the treatment plan as needed.

Summary: A 35-year-old male presented with intermittent headache and hypomnesis. The patient was diagnosed with Intermittent headache and hypomnesis. He was treated with high-dose methotrexate and idarubicin, and elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase level and cerebrospinal fluid protein concentration were noted. No follow-up plan is necessary.

A 36-year-old male patient with Wilson's disease, presenting with severe dental caries and generalized gingivitis, underwent various dental procedures to address the decay and oral health issues. Follow-up appointments with a primary care physician and regular dental check-ups are recommended to ensure the patient's overall oral health and Wilson's disease management.

Summary: A patient with cardiac hydatid cyst is undergoing surgery to remove the cyst. The patient is also prescribed bupivacain plain, inj. tramadol, and diclofenac sodium I.M. for post-operative pain management. The patient is instructed to follow up with their physician for further management.

Summary: A 55-year-old male patient is admitted for treatment of leiomyosarcoma, a rare cancer affecting the muscle layer of the wall of the abdomen and other organs. The patient is experiencing pain and numbness in the left upper limb due to the presence of an enhanced solid lesion in the apex of the left lung. He has undergone resection surgery, radiation therapy, and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for the cancer. The patient's follow-up instructions include regular check-ups with his healthcare provider to monitor his condition.

Summary: A 45-year-old female with bronchial asthma presents with multiple critical conditions, including pneumonic consolidation involving the right lower lobe, surgical emphysema, subcutaneous emphysema, air in the mediastinum, pericardium, and posterior spinal epidural space. Key findings include SPO2-89% in normal room air, 92% with 4 L/min oxygen delivered through nasal canula. Broad-spectrum antibiotics, inhalation bronchodilators, systemic corticosteroids, high-flow oxygen, and supportive measures were performed. Follow-up instructions include continued monitoring of symptoms, regular follow-up with primary care physician, and consultation with a pulmonologist as needed.

Summary: The patient has rheumatoid arthritis, an allergic skin disease, and a history of allergic reactions to Ayurvedic medication. The patient is undergoing treatment with Agnitundi vati, Valuka Sweda, and Dashanga Lepa. The patient's follow-up instructions include updating the treating physician of any future allergic reactions, maintaining a record of allergies and medications, and returning to the treating physician if symptoms develop.

Summary: Patient presents with a complex combination of Streptococcus salivarius meningitis, Antiphospholipid syndrome, cerebrospinal fluid leak (CSF-L), ventriculitis, and encephalopathy. Intravenous dexamethasone, cefepime, vancomycin, bilateral endoscopic ethmoid repair with lumbar drain placement, and intrathecal antibiotics were performed. Follow-up instructions include routine monitoring of antiphospholipid syndrome and CSF-L, continued apixaban as prescribed, and close monitoring for signs of bleeding.

Summary: A 12-year-old female with a history of SLE and JIA is admitted with complicated polyarthritis and MAS. She is treated with IVIG, high dose ASA, and IVMP, followed by low-dose Prednisone. Follow-up appointments are necessary with Rheumatology and Cardiology.

Summary:

The patient has been diagnosed with recurrence of metastatic germ cell tumor and acute megakaryoblastic leukemia. The patient also has pancytopenia, with a total leukocyte count of 3000/μl and platelet count of 20,000/μl. A bone marrow trephine biopsy and fine needle aspiration of a cervical lymph node were performed, and the patient is currently on daunorubicin and cytarabin medications for treatment. Follow-up appointments will be scheduled to monitor the patient's condition.

Summary: A 45-year-old female presents with constipation and a possible sigmoid volvulus. She is also diagnosed with hypothyroidism and microcytic anemia. Key findings include significant bowel obstruction, which was decompressed via colonoscopic procedures. Follow-up instructions include ongoing monitoring for recurrence and regular colonoscopic and laparoscopic decompressions.

Summary: Patient is experiencing an infected dentigerous cyst, along with swelling in the maxillary anterior region. The primary diagnosis is an infected cyst. The patient's secondary condition is swelling, and there are critical lab abnormalities including dull, throbbing pain. No medications were prescribed. The procedure performed was surgical enucleation of the lesion and removal of the impacted mesiodent. Follow-up instructions include maintaining good oral hygiene and scheduling follow-up visits with their dental care provider.

Summary: A 50-year-old female patient was diagnosed with rectal carcinoma. She received neoadjuvant chemotherapy with 5-FU and subsequently experienced a transient ischemic attack (TIA). She was advised to follow up with her oncologist for future management plan discussions and to seek emergency medical attention for similar symptoms.

Summary:
The patient is a 65-year-old male presenting with a femur fracture and age-related osteoporosis. He is also experiencing hip pain, swelling, and restricted mobility. Following a hemisphere replacement arthroplasty performed via posterior approach with a cemented bipolar prosthesis, the patient is currently asymptomatic with a favorable outcome. A post-operative X-ray shows a new femoral head with a longer offset assembled to the old femoral stem.

Summary: A 55-year-old male with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) presenting with stage IV NSCLC, EGFR exon 19 deletion mutation, MET amplification, PD-L1 positivity, high tumor mutational burden, and pembrolizumab and pemetrexed chemotherapy, was discharged with gefitinib 250mg per os QD, crizotinib 250mg per os BID, pemetrexed 800 mg IV every 28 days, and six cycles of chemotherapy. Follow-up instructions include regular clinical and radiographic assessments to maintain improved quality of life with no pulmonary symptoms.

Initial Clinical Summary:

A 45-year-old male patient with a history of Mesenteric ischemia secondary to atypical fibromuscular dysplasia presents with severe abdominal pain, diarrhea, and vomiting. A colonoscopy, small bowel series, magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), suboptimal angioplasty, and angioplasty with stent were performed. The patient was also prescribed medications and instructed to follow a low-fat, low-salt diet. The patient is advised to follow up with their primary care physician within one week of discharge and to schedule a follow-up appointment with their cardiologist within two weeks of discharge.

Summary:

The patient has been diagnosed with Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome, a rare vascular malformation disorder. Secondary conditions include growth retardation and abdominal swelling. Critical lab abnormalities include splenomegaly and trilineage suppression. Procedures performed include physical examination, ultrasound abdomen, and femoral angiography. Medications are not being discharged. Follow-up instructions include regular clinical evaluation and appropriate management.

Summary: A 55-year-old male patient has a recurrent schwannoma arising from the middle cranial base with sunken eye and drooping of the affected upper eyelid. He underwent an autologous ball-shaped graft and an auricular cartilage graft to correct the lower eyelid retraction and upper eyelid ptosis. The patient was advised to avoid touching the affected eye and have follow-ups as scheduled.

Summary: A 45-year-old male patient with a history of non-seminomatous germinal tumor (NSGT) E-IB and multiple sclerosis (MS) presents with increased AFP levels, increased PET scan uptake in the left supraclavicular region and both lungs, and subcutaneous interferon β-1a levels. The patient underwent left inguinal orchiectomy and subcutaneous interferon β-1a. He is currently receiving gemicitabine and oxaliplatin, and further follow-up will be at the discretion of the patient's family.

Summary:

A 45-year-old female with type 1 diabetes, absolute insulin deficiency, and hypertension is admitted to the hospital with HbA1c levels of 9.6% and 7.4%. She is currently on premixed biphasic insulin aspart, miglitol, aliskiren, and candesartan. The patient is undergoing follow-up instructions to manage her diabetes through proper diet and exercise, with no special instructions regarding diet management or physical exercise prior to and during sitagliptin treatment.

Summary: A 35-year-old male patient presenting with suspected organophosphate poisoning received atropine and parenteral hydration in the emergency department. Atropine 5 mg iv bolus and 1 mg hourly infusion, and pralidoxime were administered. Follow-up is scheduled for 6 weeks to assess the patient's routine work ability.

Summary: A 55-year-old female presented with recurrent ductal carcinoma in situ of the breast. Following a total mastectomy with immediate reconstruction and A staged DIEP flap, she has achieved a satisfactory aesthetic outcome without complications. A one-year follow-up has been scheduled for evaluation.

The patient has stage IV B mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma, which is confirmed by the presence of a myeloid sarcoma mass. Treatment involves surgical removal of the mass, radiotherapy, and two courses of high-dose cytarabine. Follow-up instructions are not provided in the note.

The patient is experiencing intentional self-harm with a primary diagnosis of deliberate self-harm. They are also diagnosed with neurological toxicity and orange-red discoloration. Key findings include pH 7.36, HCO3- 20 mmol/L, PCO2 24 mmHg, pO2 135 mmHg, Base excess -5, lactate level 2.3, and O2 saturation 100%. IV diazepam 5 mg was administered immediately, and pyridoxine 4.2 g and IV 0.9% saline are prescribed for follow-up.

Summary:

The patient is experiencing Acute Reversible Cerebral Vasoconstriction Syndrome (ARCVS), a condition characterized by vasospastic changes in blood vessels leading to decreased cerebral blood flow. The patient's primary diagnosis is ARCVS. Additional diagnoses include increased mean flow velocities (MFV) in both middle cerebral arteries, which are critical lab abnormalities. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) and Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) were performed to confirm the diagnosis. The patient is currently prescribed nimodipine for treatment. Follow-up instructions include attending follow-up appointments after completing the prescribed course of treatment.

Summary: The patient has caries in teeth and talon cusps on the maxillary left and right permanent central incisors. The patient is scheduled for restoration of these teeth at the dental office. Regular dental check-ups and oral hygiene care at home are recommended for follow-up.

Summary: A 45-year-old female patient is diagnosed with Pleomorphic Angiosarcoma (PAIS) after a pulmonary biopsy. She has two progressive lesions, one of which has undergone carboplatin and vinorelbine administration. The patient is scheduled for stereotactic radiotherapy to manage the lesions. Follow-up instructions include monitoring for any changes in symptoms and progression of the disease.

Summary: A 5-year-old child diagnosed with hemolytic uremic syndrome and norovirus. The child is experiencing leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolysis, albuminuria, and low complement levels. Continuous peritoneal dialysis is being performed. Packed red blood cells are being administered, and follow-up instructions include regular pediatrician visits and a healthy diet and lifestyle.

Initial Clinical Summary:

A 35-year-old male patient is admitted for a multi-disciplinary approach to wound management, including excision of necrotic muscles, VSD and adhesive membrane closure, negative pressure drainage equipment, stretching treatment, and intravenous antibiotic therapy. His follow-up instructions include monitoring his health and exercise preventative measures as recommended by medical professionals.

Summary: A 55-year-old male patient with isolated ACTH deficiency is undergoing pembrolizumab monotherapy for non-small cell lung cancer. Key findings include low serum cortisol and ACTH levels, hyponatremia, hypoglycemia, and inappropriate ADH secretion. He is scheduled for monthly outpatient follow-up to monitor progress and adjust treatment as needed.

Summary: The patient presented with Topiramate induced acute myopia, persistent headaches, and bilateral refractive error of -0.5 diopters. Ophthalmological examination was performed, and no further procedures were needed. The patient was advised to attend follow-up appointments with her general practitioner and ophthalmologist, and not to take Topiramate again.

Summary:

A 35-year-old female presented with symptoms of epigastric pain, vomiting, and a cystic lymphangioma originating from the left adrenal gland. A combination of ultrasonography, CT scan, and MRI were performed to diagnose the condition. The patient was diagnosed with a cystic lymphangioma and underwent surgical resection. She was advised to return to the outpatient clinic for follow-up consultations.

Summary: The patient is diagnosed with Gross Hydronephrosis (GH) caused by obstruction from a kidney stone at the junction of the ureter and renal pelvis, accompanied by renal cell transitional cell carcinoma (T2N0M0). Additional secondary conditions include abdominal girth increase, abdominal distension, intermittent nausea, and repeated intractable hiccups. The patient requires follow-up appointments with the healthcare professional for proper diet and regular check-ups.

Summary: A 55-year-old male presented with a dermoid cyst and a sinus infection. A dorsum D1 to D8 laminectomy, mid-line myelotomy, and total tumor excision under microscope were performed. He was prescribed methylprednisolone and is to follow up instructions for further evaluation and monitoring.

Summary:

This patient is undergoing treatment for multiple conditions, including low-grade neuroendocrine tumor, CLL, and marginal zone B-cell lymphoma/chronic lymphocytic leukemia. He has received R-CHOP, octreotide acetate, and CT scan procedures. Medications are currently being discharged, but he is instructed to continue following up with healthcare providers to monitor his CLL and address any future medical concerns.

Summary:

A 3-year-old female patient with known 22q11DS, cardiac anomalies, and conductive hearing loss bilaterally was evaluated. Key findings included malformed ossicular chain, narrow ear canals, epitympanic ossicular fixation on the left side, and dehiscent facial nerve canal on the left side. She underwent tympanostomy tube placement and middle ear inspection and ossicular reconstruction on the left side. Follow-up instructions include following up with the otorhinolaryngologic department and seeking regular audiology testing.

Summary: A 45-year-old male with a history of diabetes, hypertension, spinal cord injury, and empyema undergoes partial lung resection, CT scan, and empyema treatment. He is instructed to follow up with primary care physician for regular check-ups.

Summary:

The patient is experiencing a malformation complex involving severe ISH, brachycephaly, scaphocephaly, total synostosis of the sagittal suture, and severe osteolysis. The patient's follow-up instructions include a physical examination and monitoring of symptoms.
Summary: A patient diagnosed with Squamous cell carcinoma is undergoing follow-up after a clavicle fracture (CF).

Summary:

A 55-year-old male patient is admitted to the hospital with hypertension, high cholesterol, and coronary artery disease with surgical intervention. He is also experiencing cough with hemoptysis and chest discomfort. He received a computed tomography scan of the chest with contrast and a percutaneous approach with a PTFE-covered Jostent GraftMaster to address his coronary artery disease. He is currently on dual antiplatelet therapy and will follow up with the healthcare provider as scheduled.

Summary:
The patient is presenting with left knee pain and epiphyseal overgrowth, as well as left hip pain. The patient underwent surgery to resect cartilage overgrowth in the left knee, and no critical lab abnormalities are present. Follow-up sessions are scheduled at the outpatient clinic for further medical evaluations.

The patient was diagnosed with biliary colic and dyspepsia. A secondary diagnosis of colocolic intussusception was identified. There were critical lab abnormalities, including diffuse thickening of the transverse colon wall. The patient underwent a left hemicolectomy with end-to-end anastomosis. Medications were not provided during discharge. The patient was instructed to contact his primary care physician for any concerns or questions and to schedule a follow-up appointment with the surgeon within four weeks post-discharge to monitor the surgical site and assess any further symptoms.

Summary: A patient presenting with jaundice, abdominal pain, and biliary cirrhosis undergoes emergency liver transplant. Secondary conditions include hepatosplenomegaly, esophageal varices, and liver transplant. Critical lab abnormalities consist of high bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, coproporphyrin, and urophyrin. Follow-up instructions include monitoring liver function tests and managing post-operative complications.

Summary:

A 45-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and Brugada syndrome presented with a subdural empyema and chronic subdural hematoma. The primary diagnosis is subdural empyema with organized chronic subdural hematoma. The patient's laboratory results show normal serum C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. Craniotomy was performed and the patient is currently taking minocycline (200 mg every 12 hours) for wound healing and to monitor diabetes and Brugada syndrome. Follow-up instructions include visiting the primary care physician for wound healing and monitoring, and monitoring diabetes and Brugada syndrome.

Summary: A preterm baby with gross anomalies is presenting with narrow chest indicating lung hypoplasia, fused lower limbs, absent external genitalia, imperforate anus, single umbilical artery, bilateral renal agenesis, absence of both kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, seminal vesicles, and urethra, gastrointestinal system ending in a blind loop with meconium, and two pea-sized gonads. The baby has diabetes mellitus in the mother. Follow-up instructions are not provided.

Summary:

The patient is experiencing hypertension and a left total hip replacement due to avascular necrosis. Additionally, there are concerns about autoimmune, infectious, and malignant diseases. The patient has a necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis, which requires follow-up instructions not provided in the note.

The patient is experiencing Altered mental status, hypotension, and fever, which may be related to immunotherapy-induced RTA. Laboratory abnormalities include altered electrolytes, with a serum Na of 133 mEq/L, K of 3.1 mEq/L, and HCO3−1 of 1 mEq/L. A high BUN and Cr indicate possible renal dysfunction. The patient is also anemic with a total protein of 5.0 g/dL and low ALT and AST levels.

The patient is being discharged with sodium bicarbonate tablets to correct acidosis. The patient will follow up with nephrology and oncology as an outpatient to address the underlying cause of the altered mental status and electrolyte disturbances. Follow-up instructions include monitoring renal function and returning for further evaluation if symptoms persist.

Initial clinical summary:

Summary: 
The patient presents with a combination of myalgia, leukocytosis, neutrophilia, monocytosis, elevated C-reactive protein, ESR, and creatinine kinase. The patient's white blood cell count is >100 × 106/litre. A biopsy of the right tibialis anterior muscle was performed. The patient is prescribed medications and advised to maintain a healthy and balanced diet, follow up with the primary physician, and report any worsening symptoms.

Summary:

The patient presented with a complex medical history involving multiple conditions, including MSSA infection, Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) with severe aortic regurgitation, and an ascending aortic aneurysm. Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) was also diagnosed. To address these conditions, the patient underwent open-heart surgery with aortic valve replacement (AVR), ascending aortoplasty, and coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) with left internal mammary artery to left anterior descending artery. Additionally, the patient is on nafcillin and will require follow-up home health care to monitor recovery and complete antibiotics for 8 weeks.

Summary:

The patient is a 45-year-old female with no primary diagnoses, but several secondary conditions and critical lab abnormalities. She underwent a series of procedures and medications were discharged. Follow-up instructions include consulting her primary care physician for any future health concerns.

Summary: A 5-year-old patient with Listeria monocytogenes meningitis is being treated with intravenous amoxicillin and amikacin. The patient has an increased white blood cell count, and if another episode of bacterial meningitis occurs, additional studies including a genetic evaluation of IgM genotype would be indicated.

These conditions require ongoing management through psychotherapy and medication. Summary: A 65-year-old male patient presented with a stage MCC with lymph node involvement, squamous cell carcinoma, and metastases to pancreas and peripancreatic lymph nodes. He received a wide local excision with bilateral axillary and left pre-clavicular lymph node dissection and adjuvant radiation therapy. The patient passed away without undergoing any further treatment.

Summary: A 55-year-old female patient has been diagnosed with a nodular infiltrating papillary thyroid carcinoma following a total thyroidectomy and radioiodine therapy. She is currently undergoing ongoing monitoring and follow-up to assess long-term response and potential recurrence.

Summary: A 35-year-old female patient is presenting with systemic disorder causing violaceous plaques and fever, weight loss, and malaise. She has multiple small violaceous plaques on the forehead, chest, abdomen, back, and extremities. Laboratory results show low-grade fever, high-grade fever, weight loss, and 5 kg loss in 1 month. A skin biopsy was performed, and topical steroids and phototherapy were prescribed. Follow-up instructions include continuing medications, attending follow-up appointments, and reporting any new symptoms.

Initial Clinical Summary:

A 28-year-old male patient presented with multiple abrasions over his right thigh, lacerated wound on his right hand, and a serious ocular injury involving a deep perforated wound of the right eye. The patient's condition is considered critical due to the presence of bleeding ciliary body and a rupture of the globe.

The patient's primary diagnosis is a laceration of the right hand and eye injury. The secondary diagnosis is an evisceration. The patient's ocular injury is a critical condition that requires immediate attention.

Key findings include the presence of multiple abrasions on the right thigh, laceration on the right hand, and a deep perforated wound of the right eye. The patient is also experiencing bleeding ciliary body and a rupture of the globe.

The patient was administered a CT scan to assess the extent of the injury and a microscopic eye examination to evaluate the ocular damage. No medications were discharged.

The patient's follow-up instructions include coming regularly for follow-up.

A 55-year-old male patient is presenting with aortic insufficiency and ascending aortic dilatation. He has been experiencing exertional dyspnea and coughing. His lab results indicate low blood pressure (100/50 mmHg) and an elevated heart rate (80 beats/min). Chest X-ray was performed and no follow-up instructions were provided.

Summary:

A 28-year-old male presented with a 2-week history of fever, arthralgia, and skin lesions consistent with leukocytoclastic vasculitis (HSP). Secondary diagnosis was a pulmonary infection caused by Staphylococcus aureus. Elevated C reactive protein and low albumin levels indicate underlying inflammation and protein deficiency. Pulmonary aspiration smear and post-bronchoscopy sputum examination were performed to rule out other conditions. Colchicin was administered to manage pain and articular swelling. Follow-up is scheduled for three and six months with regular imaging and monitoring for recurrence or complications.

Summary:

A 65-year-old male presented with a month-long febrile illness and a history of complete atrioventricular block. The patient was diagnosed with a new vegetation attached to the pacemaker lead, septum, and tricuspid valve. He underwent TEE, open-heart surgery, and epicardial pacemaker implantation. Follow-up instructions were not provided.

Initial Clinical Summary:

A 35-year-old male patient presents with a 2-week history of paraesthesia affecting the lateral thigh. The primary diagnosis is Meralgia paresthetica. Secondary conditions and critical lab abnormalities are not reported. A Nerve Conduction Study was performed and medications discharged are Pregabalin 75-mg nocte. Follow-up instructions are to review in the clinic 4 months after the onset of the symptom and report that the paraesthesia had resolved completely and spontaneously.
